rationale: Falls or dizziness occurred once in each arm of an Alzheimer curcumin trial. Mouse rotarod latency and human balance measures do not provide Parkinson fall frequency after ground turmeric.
A turmeric-containing granule lowered a secondary speech-fluency rating. The Parkinson formulation studies provide no ground-turmeric effect on voice volume.
Automated animal gait and composite human scales cover related motor outcomes. The walking-speed pilot supplies no freezing episodes. No ground-turmeric freezing frequency estimate.
UPDRS Part IV and a motor examination during OFF are distinct from daily hours OFF. The primary trial sources give no ground-turmeric duration estimate.
Renal trials gave mixed olfactory component results, and two COVID cases reported improvement after combined extracts. No grated-turmeric Parkinson olfaction result.
The human Parkinson trial reports aggregate clinical scales and the older-adult study measured pegboard dexterity. Neither estimates grated turmeric and handwriting size.

Turmeric extract produced a selective eye-tracking attention signal. Whole-turmeric capsules and curry reports assessed related cognitive outcomes outside Parkinson. No grated-turmeric Parkinson comparison.

A Parkinson nanomicelle trial favored global sleep quality. A separate curcumin Epworth trial outside Parkinson was inconclusive. Neither measured daytime sleepiness after grated turmeric in Parkinson.
